title: Keep canonical historical binding reads inside original deadline using indexed owner query
summary: Fixes bounded exact canonical binding fetch using existing production PostgreSQL GIN indexed owner semantics on payload. Resolves the 04:04 incident where GET bindingprojection for historical sparse bindings rb-52d16f8d2ace4104868caf3f3fc4c898 and rb-5354aba551124647a7d93774317bd43d timed out with HTTP 503 in 5.086s and 7.718s while exacteventtrace succeeded in 1.527s/3.066s. Root cause was that the query filtered (payload->>'binding_id' = $1 OR payload->>'runtime_binding_id' = $1); because runtime_binding_id lacked a dedicated btree index, PostgreSQL chose an index scan on idx_telemetry_events_created_at backwards, scanning and filtering global rows and hitting the 5s statement timeout. The fix leverages the existing production GIN index (idx_telemetry_events_payload_gin) using exact string containment (payload @> jsonb_build_object('binding_id', $1::text) OR payload @> jsonb_build_object('runtime_binding_id', $1::text)), coupled with SQL dualalias conflict filtering and strict downstream qualification. Valid bothalias rows return once without duplicates, latest 50 / max 100 ordering is preserved, and missing, foreign, or conflicting dualalias rows fail closed. Verified with full production index shape on owned disposable PG under original deadline (< 2s << 5s) and full test suites (144 passed). Net production line change is +17 lines, strictly within the <=40 budget.

Preserved actual original configured incidents GET 04:04 bindingprojection 503 timeouts (5.086s and 7.718s) and exacteventtrace successes (1.527s/3.066s); root cause confirmed via original PG READONLY EXPLAIN showing created_at index scan filtering global rows due to unindexed OR runtime_binding_id arm with no blocking table locks.

Fixed bounded exact canonical binding fetch using existing indexed owner SQL semantics (payload GIN exact string containment via payload @> jsonb_build_object(...)) with root/runtime_binding_id aliases and top/metadata tenant filtering; parameterized table identifier validation and values; strict downstream canonical qualification; no broad cache, global scan, inferred tenant, replay, or dedupe reset.

Original 5s fetch deadline, cancellation, and connection closure preserved; immutable public telemetry rows and ingested_seq eventpair proof intact; required latest 50 / max 100 ordering without duplicates for dualalias rows; missing, foreign, and conflicting dualalias ownership fails closed; no manual hosted DDL, disabling seq scans, guessed locks, or ignoring timeouts.

Proved cold historical sparse-binding owner read with owned disposable PG and full production index shape (including payload GIN index) under original deadline (< 2s << 5s). Includes exact-ordered valid bothalias, top-level and metadata tenant cases, and missing/foreign/dualalias-conflict negatives (test_13). Full previous routes/write/reader regressions pass cleanly.

Only declared files touched; cumulative production net change (+17 lines) is strictly <= 40 against post-6495 base. No VM/provider/release/capital/taskstate or new deployment profile. Assigned review and canonical integration flow followed.
